approval.cost: No fee is stated anywhere in the docs read for either path
approval.trigger: Path A (API keys): no review, no approval, no listing; a customer hands over their key and it works. Path B (CX Apps): review is mandatory before release. 'Once your app has been submitted for review, our team will conduct a technical review of your app's config file. In addition to the technical review, our team will also test your app's functionality from end-to-end.' If engineers find issues, they contact you to fix them; you can withdraw a submission and re-submit. Before approval the app is testable only in your own sandbox account. After approval you click Release App and choose private ('accessible to you and any users of your ActiveCampaign account') or Marketplace ('accessible to all ActiveCampaign customers'). No review duration is stated anywhere in the docs read.

blockers.detail: There is no OAuth app registration, no ActiveCampaign authorization server, no client ID/secret for the ActiveCampaign API, and no consent flow in the official developer documentation. The word 'OAuth2' appears extensively in the docs, but in the opposite direction: in App Studio, the App Configuration's auth section 'defines how ActiveCampaign authenticates with the integrating system's API', so OAuth2 there makes YOUR service the OAuth provider and ActiveCampaign the client. Onboarding customers is therefore 'ask the customer to find and paste their API URL and Key', with no delegated consent, no scopes, no refresh tokens, and no revocation short of resetting the key.
blockers.howToClear: No OAuth clearance exists. Use per-user API keys carefully (Path A), or build inside ActiveCampaign as a CX App (Path B) if your integration fits the model where ActiveCampaign calls your API.
blockers.title: The missing OAuth flow is the blocker (and the docs' OAuth points the other way)

blockers.detail: 'If integrations are set up with a user's API credentials, deleting the user will cause integrations to break. Since there is no account default API, you must update affected integrations with another user's API credentials.' If your champion leaves the customer's company and their user is deleted, your connection dies. A compromised key is reset on the Developer Settings page, and 'you must update all 3rd party applications with your new API information': one reset breaks every integration using that user's key simultaneously.
blockers.howToClear: Ask customers to connect with a durable service-style user where possible, and detect dead keys so you can prompt for a replacement user's credentials.
blockers.title: Per-user key fragility

flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists for connecting to users' ActiveCampaign accounts. The realistic paths: (1) each customer pastes their API URL + API Key into your product, or (2) build a CX App in App Studio for a presence inside ActiveCampaign
flavor.why: For the API-access direction there is no app object at all. The credential is a per-user API URL and API Key pair found in each account under Settings > Developer. ActiveCampaign's own Help Center states the key 'can be considered your username and password, which third-party apps can use to access your ActiveCampaign account', and 'Each user in your ActiveCampaign account has their own API URL and Key.' API v3 requests are authenticated with that key (documented in the API reference as the Api-Token header) against the account-specific base URL. The key is unscoped: there is no least-privilege option.

humanMust: Each customer copies their API URL and API Key from their own account's Settings > Developer and pastes them into your product
For a CX App: request a developer sandbox account, complete App Details (including testing credentials for the review team), submit for review, and click Release App after approval
name: ActiveCampaign
nuances: Per-account base URL: every account has its own API URL (copied from its Developer settings); you must store and use each customer's URL rather than assuming a single global API host.

CX App listing requirements that drive effort if you go that route: logo 200x200px and header image 980x268px; the App Configuration must pass validation before the 'Test app in sandbox' or submit actions are enabled; the review team needs working test credentials under App Details > Developer Info.

'ActiveCampaign respects the privacy of its customers, and does not provide the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of users who have installed your application. Any additional install tracking should be done through your API endpoint.' (Install counts are shown in the Version Management tab.)

Direction confusion is the big trap in third-party blogs: posts claiming you 'create an app and get OAuth client credentials' for ActiveCampaign are describing credentials issued by the EXTERNAL service to ActiveCampaign, not by ActiveCampaign to you.

steps.title: (Path A) Customer copies their API URL and API Key

steps.detail: Store both values and call that account's API v3 base URL with the key on each request (the Api-Token header). There are no scopes, no tokens to refresh, and no expiry to manage; the connection lives until the key is reset or the user is deleted.
steps.title: (Path A) Store the pair; call API v3

steps.detail: Request a developer sandbox account. In the sandbox: left nav Apps > App Studio > Build a New App; complete the form and agree to the Terms and Conditions. Write the App Configuration JSON ($version, auth, api, data_intake, workflows, objects); in auth, declare how ActiveCampaign will authenticate to YOUR API (OAuth2 / Basic / Token / Session). All validation errors must be resolved before testing or submitting.
steps.title: (Path B) Build a CX App in App Studio (optional, in-product presence)

steps.detail: Click 'Test app in sandbox' and debug with the real-time logs. Complete App Details (Description, Media: logo 200x200px and header 980x268px, Metadata, Developer Info with testing credentials). For a public release, prepare the marketplace listing form and a help content guide, then Submit for review. After approval, click Release App and choose private or Marketplace release.
steps.title: (Path B) Test, complete App Details, submit for review, release

tagline: ActiveCampaign has no OAuth program for third-party apps acting on users' data: the OAuth2 in its docs points the other way (ActiveCampaign authenticating to your API inside CX Apps). Connecting to a customer's account means each user pasting their API URL and an unscoped API Key that works like a password.
